textRun.content: Does an explicit physical estimate help the robot adapt better than predicting useful control settings directly?
Act under unfamiliar or changing physical conditions.
My idea: observations + environmental estimates → policy → action.
When behavior differs from expectation, revise the assumptions.
First scope: pick-and-place with unknown object mass.
Motion clusters did not consistently capture failure causes.
Groups were tuning-sensitive and split apparently similar causes.
Outcomes overlapped across settings and random seeds.
A single failure did not reliably identify which parameter to change.
Appearance → mass estimate → conditioned policy → action.
Appearance + task → initial control settings → action.
Humans prepare forces from appearance, then adjust with experience.
Predict mass before interaction; control other physical variables.
Explore direct prediction, distributions, or shape + material reasoning.
Appearance must contain mass information; identical images cannot reveal random mass changes.
Evaluate estimation quality and first-attempt picking success.
First step: an initial visual estimate
Retain observations and actions across attempts.
Learn when to revise estimates, which to change, and by how much.
Explore memory state versus a fixed base + retained weight changes.
Goal: reuse useful experience in future encounters.
Proposed direction: the complete adaptation loop is not yet demonstrated.

structuredContent.title: robots that adapt by forming assumptions about their environment and refining them through experience
